references.text: Continuation of the instructions concerning the onyx stones, explaining how the names are to be engraved and placed on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as a memorial for the sons of Israel.
Fulfillment of the command in Exodus 28:9, where Bezalel actually makes the onyx stones with the names of the sons of Israel engraved upon them.
The first mention of the onyx stone (shoham) in the Bible, in connection with the land of Havilah.
The onyx stone is mentioned as a precious gem that cannot be compared to the value of wisdom.
David gathered onyx stones for the building of the temple, showing the stone's significance in a holy context.
The list of the sons of Israel (the sons of Jacob) whose names were to be engraved on the stones.
The twelve sons of Israel (Jacob) to whom the names refer.
In the new Jerusalem, the names of the twelve tribes are written on the gates, reflecting how the names were carried on the priest's garment.
Confirmation that the instruction concerning the onyx stones was completed exactly as it had been given.
Describes the actual execution of the engraving on the onyx stones as a seal.
Confirms that the twelve names on the stones were correctly executed according to God's original instruction.
Theological reflection: The priests carry the people's names before God (Exodus), while they also carry God's name over the people (Numbers).
